entries.model: MiniMax H3 (FL2VA, sampler PDD 8-step por defecto)
entries.time_measured: PDD 8-step vs 20 steps (A/B same prompt/seed, 5090): 5 s 480p 58.7 s -> 35.9 s (1.63x). SageAttention H3 (bench 1344x768, 362 frames, 20 steps): 30m21s PyTorch -> 14m44s (2.06x, no clear visual degradation). VAE int8 (default 2026-10-06): A/B 8 s 720p PDD-8 clip 138.5 s -> 111.0 s; VAE ~2.2x encoding, 1.4-2.7x decoding. Native output 768p/24 fps with jointly generated 32 kHz stereo audio.
entries.quality_notes: Default engine of the stack: maximum local visual and audiovisual quality. Native stereo audio co-generated; Spanish among the 11 stable dialogue languages (official notation (S1)/<d>[Spanish]...</d>). PDD 8-step with no visible degradation and dialogue present (A/B); fail-closed recipe 4/6/8 steps, euler, sigma shift 12/3. VAE int8 approved as default for speed: subtly lower micro-detail than fp16 and slight banding in gradients, no serious artifacts (--h3-vae fp16 for masters). Disk note: official BF16 weights ~288 GB in the repo; local pruned int8 install: FL2VA 21 GB + video VAE int8 2.8 GB + PDD LoRAs + text encoder qwen3vl_32b nvfp4 (no measurement of the local total). VRAM: dynamic fill via weight staging on the reference 32 GB 5090.
entries.when_not_to_use: Do not exceed 15 s per render (production range 4-15 s; 15 s at 2K OOMs the 32 GB 5090). Never let H3 render on-screen text: it invents/distorts it (add text with ffmpeg drawtext in post). Community Turbo-LoRAs ruled out for the cinematic series (ghosting/posterization/broken audio). If you only need to iterate prompts fast without references, LTX 2.5/2.3 are faster.

entries.time_measured: 720p 3 s measured on RTX 5090 (2026-08-27): t2v 45 s, i2v 44 s, flf2v 61 s; 1080p ~2x slower. Fixed 24 fps; fixed sigmas schedule (ignores --steps). VRAM/disk not measured on the spec sheet.
entries.quality_notes: Quality between H3 and LTX 2.3: faster than H3 with better prompt adherence and better audio than 2.3. Video + stereo audio generated jointly. Official two-stage pipeline (half res -> LTXVLatentUpsampler x2 -> refine), frame grid 8k+1.
entries.when_not_to_use: The script rejects --audio, --lipsync, --id-lora, --reference-audio, --reference-image/-video: no audio conditioning, no lip-sync and no identity references. For identity across shots or exact audio, use H3 Ref2VA. Prefer 720p for iterating (1080p ~2x cost).

entries.model: LTX 2.3 (22B dev + distilled LoRA 384 v1.1 + spatial upscaler x2 v1.1)
entries.time_measured: Spec-sheet estimates (2026-03-08): 5 s @720p 1-3 min; 10 s 2-4 min; 20 s 3-8 min (no exact per-step measurement). Two passes: structure at half res + latent upscale + refine. Partial known disk: distilled LoRA ~7.1 GB + spatial upscaler ~950 MB (base 22B checkpoint with no declared size).
entries.quality_notes: Fast fallback of the stack. Generates intelligible voice and dialogue with simple formatting (single quotes: he is yelling 'text' + language/accent); ambient audio co-generated. Limits: --duration max 20 s; recommended 4-7 s (96-168 frames), >257 frames accumulates artifacts. v1.1: cleaner audio and better micro-textures.
entries.when_not_to_use: Quality below H3 (that is why it is the fallback). Unreliable camera moves (zoom/pan/tilt); the higher the resolution, the less movement; realistic people only in close-ups. Never prompt 'singing' if the shot carries its own music track (it co-generates clashing audio). Dimensions not divisible by 32 fail.
entries.workflow_ref: comfyui-local: generate_video.py --engine ltx23 --prompt '...' (--audio for rhythmic conditioning; the model regenerates the audio output)

entries.time_measured: I2V without reference video (1344x768, 362 frames, 20 steps + SageAttention): 13m45s. With PDD 8-step (default since 2026-08-31) the A/Bs measure 1.63x-2.23x depending on mode (FL2VA 5 s 480p: 58.7->35.9 s). Keyframes as real temporal anchors (17k+5 grid).
entries.quality_notes: FL2VA incorporates the keyframes as hard temporal anchors: it is the only exact visual-junction path (Ref2VA is a semantic approximation, not pixel to pixel). FL2VA animates the DELTA between the two keyframes: light or pose variations between first and last frame are animated continuously; keep the framing identical between the extremes or the model invents a camera move. Spanish supported in dialogue.
entries.when_not_to_use: Do not combine --image/--end-image with references (the native node rejects it; an image passed as a reference is still Ref2VA). FL2VA accepts no refs or exact-audio: it co-generates the soundscape (verify it does not invent voice). >15 s does not fit; H3 does not render text.

entries.time_measured: 720p 3 s measured on RTX 5090 (2026-08-27): i2v 44 s, flf2v 61 s; 1080p ~2x slower. flf2v is a single pass at full res (12-sigma) with guides at frame 0 and -1 at strength 0.7.
entries.quality_notes: Interpolation between two frames (flf2v) in a single step; native audio. Two-stage i2v with latent upscale. Ideal for animating a keyframe when multimodal identity or exact audio are not needed.
entries.when_not_to_use: No refs/identity/lipsync/exact audio (flags rejected). If the first frame must match pixel for pixel and the original audio must be kept, H3 FL2VA + post. 1080p ~2x cost: iterate at 720p.
entries.source_model_repo: Lightricks (LTX 2.5; repo HF exacto no declarado en la ficha local)

entries.time_measured: No exact time measurement on the spec sheet (not measured); optimal clips 3-8 s; [SPEECH] text up to ~10 s (>15 s truncates and degrades).
entries.quality_notes: --lipsync: separates voice with MelBand RoFormer and conditions the video on the clean voice; the output keeps the ORIGINAL audio track (replace with ffmpeg after generating). --id-lora: transfers voice identity from ~5 s of reference and synthesizes the new words ([VISUAL]/[SPEECH]/[SOUNDS]); integrated lip-sync, no separate TTS. Validated rule: --identity-guidance-scale 1.5 (default 3.0 stiffens the face); BF16 checkpoint gives better visual/lip-sync than FP8. Spanish works but with less natural pronunciation (trained in English).
entries.when_not_to_use: Do not combine --id-lora with --lipsync or --audio (it manages voice internally). ID-LoRA mode at strength 1.0 is extremely static unless you lower the guidance. Dialogues >10 s: split into clips. For lipsync over an exact master track with multi-ref visual identity, H3 Ref2VA exact-audio is superior.
entries.workflow_ref: comfyui-local: generate_video.py --engine ltx23 --lipsync --image portrait.png --audio speech.wav | --id-lora --image portrait.png --reference-audio voice.wav

entries.model: MiniMax H3 Ref2VA (hasta 9 img + 3 video + 3 audio) + exact-audio + cadena motion-context
entries.time_measured: PDD 8-step vs 20 steps (A/B, 5090): 15 s Ref2VA 1344x768 with 3 refs 914 s -> 410 s (2.23x, no visible degradation). Cost scales with the reference video (20 steps + Sage): I2V without video-ref 13m45s; Ref2VA with 10 s video 34m41s; image + 10 s video 35m12s (adding one image in 'match' mode only added 31 s); with 15 s of video-ref ~160 s/step (20 steps ~54 min, fills VRAM with spill to RAM and blows the standard timeout -> use a larger timeout and trim the ref). Motion-context chain (ComfyUI-H3-Motion-Context, validated 2026-10-19): 132-142 s/segment (736x416, 124 f, PDD); 264-290 s per 7.3 s segment @768p with refs.
entries.quality_notes: Character-consistency pattern from the reference workflow: character reference image (better an approved take IN context of the same scene/lighting, not the white-background portrait) + reference video for motion/camera + a prompt that assigns an explicit job to each tag (<Picture 1> = identity/composition; <Video 1> = camera/tempo). Identity is preserved across shots. Ref2VA is semantic/temporal conditioning, NOT pixel to pixel: it anchors the opening frame to the composition image (the prompt text loses against the image), and an extra variant of the same character causes morphing at the end of the clip (pass only the individual's ref + 'must remain the same individual' + negative morphing). exact-audio mode (--preserve-reference-audio, exactly 1 audio): conditions mouth/motion and remuxes the original track ALAC lossless -> lip-sync synchronized by construction with the master song. --h3-chain chain: continues the latent (image+sound) of the previous segment, 9/10 visual junction with no pose jump; the co-generated audio 'is reborn' at the junction (~2-3 clips are deafening): policy <=15 s monolith, chain only for >15 s/one-takes, and the final track ALWAYS remuxed from the master.
entries.when_not_to_use: Exact junctions (identical first frame): use FL2VA --image, not Ref2VA. Budgets: <=9 images, <=3 videos (2-15 s each, total <=15 s), <=3 audios (total <=15 s), <=12 files; not combinable with first/last frame. The audio of reference videos consumes the first <Audio N> tags. Avoid 15 s video refs on a 32 GB 5090 if a 10 s one suffices. Do not assign contradictory functions to two refs.
entries.workflow_ref: comfyui-local: generate_video.py --engine minimax-h3 --reference-image char.png --reference-video motion.mp4 --prompt 'Use <Picture 1> for identity and <Video 1> for camera/timing...' | exact-audio: --reference-audio master.wav --preserve-reference-audio | chain: --h3-chain N --chain-prompts-json (rules in references/minimax-h3-guide.md)

entries.model: NVIDIA DLSS SR 3x + DLSS 5 NR (nodos ComfyUI, runtime NGX real)
entries.time_measured: Measured on RTX 5090 (2026-10-15, 5 s windows 1344x768): NR 1x DLAA ~14 fps of frames (~9 s/clip); 3x upscale+NR ~7-8 fps (~16 s/clip); FG->60: 34 s @768p, 215 s @4K. Full 274 s master (pipeline v2): 3x upscale+NR ~12 min + FG 24->60 per shot (59 shots) ~5 h + HDR 1500 nits ~57 min + HDR10 encode ~13 min ~= 6 h. 30 s end-to-end A/B: 28 min. HDR: ~9 min per 30 s of 4K60 (chunks <=120 f, ~87 s/chunk).
entries.quality_notes: 4K default since the 2026-10-15 A/B: DLSS 3x+NR beats Lanczos (sharper and cleaner, no ringing). NR reconstructs materials (skin/hair/fabric) with preset M + automatic_mask + skin 2.0 + structure 1.5; it does NOT recover faces the source lost. At 3x the NR always does the documented fallback (SR first, NR at output res). Pipeline v2 approved (2026-10-16): H3 768p -> DLSS 3x+NR (4032x2304, crop 16:9 and scale to 3840x2160) -> FG 60 per shot -> RTX Video HDR (PQ, mastering 1500 nits) -> HDR10 10-bit. Hard cuts: pre-split mandatory at calibrated cuts (dip SSIM 32x32 UNION of edit boundaries; FG's internal detector missed an obvious cut and melted frames). Lip drift: FG per shot rounds +0.5 f/shot -> trim to a global 60 fps grid (m60_fix.py) or ~200 ms of desync at the end of the master. HDR10 verification: re-encode yuv420p10le + bt2020/smpte2084 (a plain -c copy does not write the VUI tags); for YouTube, HEVC main10 + ST 2086 metadata + MaxCLL (yt_hdr10_upload.sh), otherwise YouTube treats it as SDR.
entries.when_not_to_use: Requires an RTX 40/50 GPU (NGX runtime) with exclusive GPU access; no GPU/broker => Lanczos (ffmpeg). RTXTrueHDR is an image batch (chunking <=120 f at 4K60). If the user does not explicitly ask for HDR, the default delivery is a controlled SDR Rec.709 tone-map (YouTube's tone-map washes out the colors and the HDR badge is not guaranteed).

entries.time_measured: No time measurement on the spec sheet (not measured); only size verified: 4:30 master @24 fps at CRF15 preset slow -> ~823 MB (~24 Mbps). Slow 4K encode: always run in background.
entries.quality_notes: Prioritizes temporal stability and naturalness over artificial sharpness on footage already generated by AI (it does not duplicate AI artifacts). Lost the 2026-10-15 A/B against DLSS 3x+NR and remains as fallback. Scale-then-crop chain for non-16:9 sources (1344x768 -> scale 3840x2196 lanczos -> crop 3840x2160), stretch <=0.07%. Single pass, 24 fps master with audio as reference.
entries.when_not_to_use: If a GPU/broker is available: DLSS 3x+NR is the default. Do not chain Lanczos in stages (720p->1080p->4K). Not Real-ESRGAN by default (AI upscalers add artifacts over AI footage). Pipeline order: 4K first over the 24 fps master, then interpolation to 60 fps.
entries.license: MIT (documented pipeline); ffmpeg as external dependency
entries.workflow_ref: video-4k-upscale: ffmpeg -i in.mp4 -vf 'scale=3840:2196:flags=lanczos,crop=3840:2160:0:18' -c:v libx264 -preset slow -crf 15 -pix_fmt yuv420p -c:a copy -movflags +faststart out_4k.mp4

entries.model: Open-H3-Regenerate-2K (LoRA merged rank 576 + latent upscaler 3D; 3 pasos Euler)
entries.time_measured: Measured on RTX 5090 (base int8 convrot + LoRA merged): 5 s @1920x1088: 178-187 s; 5 s @2560x1440: 290-297 s; 9.4 s @2K WITHOUT the SageAttention patch: ~15 min, clean (sharpness ~1200-1889 vs draft ~670). 15 s @2K: OOM (convrot64 shared memory) -> split ~7.5 s per camera move or refine at 1080p. Known disk: LoRA merged 8.8 GB + latent upscaler 0.69 GB.
entries.quality_notes: Open alternative to the closed H3-Regenerate-2K (API): it REGENERATES detail at the target res in 3 Euler steps (sigmas [0.909375, 0.857143, 0.666667, 0], CFG 1) over the 384P-768P draft; layout/motion/color stay locked by the draft. It is regeneration: identity QA mandatory on every clip. CRITICAL PITFALL: the MiniMaxH3MemoryEfficientSageAttentionPatch (KJNodes) memory patch CORRUPTS clips >5 s on this route (int8 Q/K + fp8 V quantization degrades with sequence length: 5 s correct, 9.4 s comes out as uniform blur/grid with no error at all; forcing fp32 accumulation does not fix it) -> direct wiring for clips >124 frames. Identity drift: the official sigma 0.909 buys maximum detail but reinterprets micro-attributes and, in shots with several characters, an entire species/anatomy; rule: lower sigma before changing identity, free chroma anchor (mergeplanes Y from the refine + Cb/Cr from the draft) and short prompt per shot (never the long generation prompt).
entries.when_not_to_use: Native 4K unfeasible on the 5090: 4K route = refine @2560x1440 -> DLSS 1.5x+NR -> 4K (FG/HDR unchanged). ALWAYS feed the original draft clip, never frames taken from an already scaled/encoded master. Do not stack PDD/Turbo on top of the LoRA merged (it already includes the distillations). VRAM is the limiting factor, not time: the refine runs at the target res (the latent upscaler 'saves time, not VRAM'); always smoke 1080p -> 2K. Do not use it if non-generative reconstruction suffices: DLSS SR+NR is cheaper.

entries.time_measured: Measured on RTX 5090 (2026-10-15): FG->60 34 s per 5 s clip @768p; 215 s @4K (~43x the source duration). In the 274 s master it dominates the total cost (~5 h of the ~6 h of pipeline v2). Quality-untested option: FG at 768p before the upscale (6x faster).
entries.quality_notes: Won the A/B against AMT-L (2026-10-15) and passed CFR+quality at 4K: exact CFR verified over sorted pts (24->60 is the native DLSSG case; a 24->120->60 gives the same phase grid at ~2.7x the cost). It is ~4x slower per frame than upscale+NR because the post-video must estimate dense optical flow (in a game the engine gives the vectors for free). JSON reports on disk confirm the neural pass (generated_frames/copied_frames/scene_cuts).
entries.when_not_to_use: No RTX 40/50 GPU with NGX => AMT-L. NEVER interpolate across a hard cut: pre-split mandatory at calibrated cuts (FG's internal detector is unreliable on hard cuts and produces 'melted' frames). After FG per shot, trim to the global 60 grid (m60_fix.py) ALWAYS in multi-shot masters or the lip drift accumulates (~+217 ms in 274 s). The worker requires an exclusive GPU.

entries.time_measured: A/B 3 s (2026-08-18): route 24->96->60 (2 passes 2x) vs 24->120->60 (5x pass): perfect identical CFR (178 packets @60, 0 outliers), mean pixel diff 1.68/255 (below the CRF16 noise floor), visually 'practically indistinguishable'; the 5x pass does 4 inferences/pair vs 3 (~33% more GPU with no measurable gain). Final 4K60 encode >7 min (background). 4K master 24->96: 6480 f -> 25917 f, 1.1 GB.
entries.quality_notes: AMT-L resolves movement artifacts that AMT-S and RIFE left behind (shimmer in slow orbits). Method: interpolate ABOVE the target (96 or 120) and decimate to 60 => every frame is truly interpolated, clean CFR without duplicates. Recommended route 2-pass 24->48->96->60. Calibrated SSIM cut-list (isolated-dip rule <0.60 with neighbor >0.62) mandatory: do not interpolate across hard cuts (ghosting).
entries.when_not_to_use: With a NGX GPU/broker available, DLSS FG is the approved default (faster and better A/B). Do not interpolate to 48 and then resample to 60 (it would duplicate frames -> dirty pacing). Model requires H/W divisible by 16 after --scale. The 5x/8x demos use a GoPro-trained ckpt: A/B first.
entries.workflow_ref: video-fps-interpolation: ssim_calibrate.py -> amt_interp.py --passes 2 --cut-list ... -> ffmpeg fps=60 -> final encode with audio from the 24 fps master

entries.model: Programa frame(t)->imagen: Canvas 2D / SVG+CSS / Three.js / GLSL / Manim / Remotion / p5.js + captura headless Chromium -> MP4
entries.time_measured: No global measurement (not measured); validated design budget: <=300 ms/frame at full res => ~15 min per full render of 100 s @30 fps; long renders in parallel chunks (--start/--frames) and lossless concat.
entries.quality_notes: Verified determinism: the same t produces the same image in any order (loop_probe.js hash-probes seeks and checks loop periodicity). Deliverable MP4 verified with check_video.sh (resolution, fps, duration, frame count, codec, pix_fmt, audio streams, black/frozen segments) + VERIFY.md line by line against the SPEC. Encoding compatible: libx264 -pix_fmt yuv420p -crf 18 -preset medium -movflags +faststart; AAC 48 kHz audio mastered ~-16/-14 LUFS. Zero dependency on AI GPU: everything drawn by code (motion graphics, diagrams, simulations, 3D, loops).
entries.when_not_to_use: Not generative AI: it does not produce photorealism, characters or scenes from text (for that H3/LTX). If Chromium will not start or WebGL falls back to software, do not fight it: switch to @napi-rs/canvas or Manim. Do not reproduce content with fictitious data: only the strings and figures from the SPEC.
